name: Starlink VisorSat
note: Benchmarking M4 reference model for Mallama (2021). V1.x chassis in 'shark-fin' operational mode with the deployable visor. Body frame: +Z nadir, +X toward the Sun's azimuth (the bus yaws so the visor stays sunward), +Y = +Z x +X. Every number is covered by `sources`; the visor's scale is calibrated (see its source), the materials are presets.

sources.value: bus 1.3 x 2.8 m footprint, 0.2 m thick
sources.source: Footprint: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim (V1.5 row: bus 2.8 x 1.3 m; V1.0 'about 3 m bus', same chassis family). Thickness: 60-satellite stack of 6.7 m in the Falcon 9 fairing (lilibots.blogspot.com, 2020-04, secondary estimate).

sources.subject: antennas
sources.value: white antenna region 0.9 x 2.2 m centred on the nadir face (63% of the base); range 40-80%
sources.source: Cole 2021 (arXiv:2107.06026) section 2: 'white antenna panels on the base', base otherwise polished metal. Region size not published.

sources.subject: visor
sources.value: black sheet 1.45 x 2.2 m under the antenna region, reaching 0.55 m sunward of the antennas' edge (0.35 m past the bus side), 0.233 m below the base
sources.source: Radio-transparent foam that blocks sunlight from the antennas (SpaceX via Tesmanian 2020, SpaceNews 2020). Cole 2021 section 3.2: antennas fully shaded at 23 deg Sun depression, light leaks under at smaller angles - so gap = inset x tan 23 deg (derived). The scale is unpublished and was FITTED (benchmarking M8, 2026-09-23): inset scanned 0.2-0.9 m against the mallama2021_visorsat phase curve (10-deg bins with >= 10 observations), minimum RMS 0.14 mag at 0.55 m (0.42 at the earlier 0.2 m guess). That curve is therefore a fit residual for this model; the held-out checks are the mallama2020a V1.0 mean and the visorsat_vs_original differential.

sources.subject: solar_array
sources.value: one 2.8 x 8.1 m array, cells facing the Sun's azimuth
sources.source: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim (V1.5: solar array 2.8 x 8.1 m). Hinge at the centre of the bus top: estimate.

sources.subject: bus
sources.value: base to nadir, visor side yawed to the Sun's azimuth
sources.source: Cole 2021 section 2 ('base and its antennas face the Earth') and section 5 ('the visor must remain pointing to the Sun-azimuth for it to work'); SpaceX 'shark-fin' operational mode (Tesmanian 2020).

sources.subject: array
sources.value: fixed 24 deg from local vertical, top leaning away from the Sun (95% range 14-34 deg)
sources.source: Cole 2021 Table 3 (late-2020 fit, the Mallama 2021 period): panel offset angle 24 deg away from Sun azimuth, fixed to the local vertical rather than Sun-tracking (section 4.2 item 3). June 2021 data fit -5 deg instead (section 6).

sources.subject: bus_metal
sources.source: Cole 2021 section 2: base is 'polished metal'. Table 3 specular beam exponents 24 and 52 -> GGX alpha = sqrt(2/(n+2)) = 0.28 and 0.19, geometric mean 0.23. That alpha is the Beckmann equivalence, but GGX is kept: with Beckmann tails the M8 phase curve came out 0.3-0.5 mag fainter at 70-110 deg (GGX's longer tail is the base light seen off the specular beam). F0 and diffuse albedo: preset estimates.

sources.subject: antenna_white
sources.source: Cole 2021 section 2: 'white antenna panels'. Albedo not published (Phase 3c).
Cole 2021 Figure 2 (black edges added on visorsats) and section 3.2 ('the visor is declared as being black').

sources.subject: array_back_dark
sources.source: Cole 2021 Table 3: rear-face emission b = 0, section 4.2: rear face < 20% of the base.
